body:
## RED at HEAD — the builder is pinned to the wire truth and fails loud

The self-test now fixtures the artifacts Tauri v2 ACTUALLY emits (read from the v0.2.1 release run 42816215486 build logs: `Finished 3 updater signatures at: ...deb.sig / ...AppImage.sig / ...rpm.sig` — v2 signs the INSTALLERS themselves; only macOS wraps in `.app.tar.gz`; the v1 wrappers `.AppImage.tar.gz`/`.nsis.zip`/`.msi.zip` never occur). The old self-test named the v1 fiction and passed — a gate that tested a story, not the wire.

The new pins fail at HEAD exactly as the issue predicts:

```
TypeError: build() got an unexpected keyword argument 'darwin_arch'
```

— the macOS bundle's arch was UNDECLARED (the product names it `IUM.app.tar.gz`, no arch), the shape heuristic guessed `darwin-x86_64`, and no shipped hardware reports that key. Next pins after the signature: the AppImage and the NSIS `.exe` must become `linux-x86_64` / `windows-x86_64` entries (v2 serves them directly), and an `.app.tar.gz` whose arch was never declared must fail the build (`UNKEYED`) instead of guessing.

Fix next: `build()` takes `--darwin-arch` (the build leg's knowledge, never a filename guess), `parse_name` learns the real v2 shapes (installers are the updater artifacts), and `release_collect.sh` ships the installer `.sig` sidecars so the pairing rule can hold. The release then re-drives from the re-tagged v0.2.1.
